policy: Primary papers, official benchmark pages, and formal surveys only; descriptions are paraphrases, not quotations.

sources.title: TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents
verified_evidence: The benchmark couples multi-day planning with six tools and a sandbox of roughly four million records.

Its analysis identifies incomplete information collection, tool errors, multi-constraint tracking, long-horizon degradation, global budget/minimum-night failures, and mismatch between reasoning and action.

sources.title: ChinaTravel: An Open-Ended Travel Planning Benchmark with Compositional Constraint Validation for Language Agents
verified_evidence: ChinaTravel adds open-ended Chinese requirements, a fixed travel sandbox, and a compositional DSL for feasibility, constraint satisfaction, and preference comparison.
The official neuro-symbolic pipeline separates natural-language-to-DSL translation from interactive search, making representation quality a distinct planning concern.

sources.title: Understanding the Planning of LLM Agents: A Survey
verified_evidence: The survey organizes LLM-agent planning methods into task decomposition, multi-plan selection, external-module aid, reflection/refinement, and memory augmentation.

sources.title: Large Language Models for Planning: A Comprehensive and Systematic Survey
verified_evidence: The survey separates external-module-augmented, finetuning-based, and search-based approaches and distinguishes open-loop from closed-loop planning.
It treats environment understanding, logical reasoning, sequential decision making, evaluation, and external planners as connected parts of LLM planning.

sources.title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models
verified_evidence: ReAct interleaves reasoning traces with environment actions so observations can update plans and support exception handling.
Environment interaction converts planning from isolated generation into a feedback-conditioned loop.

sources.title: LLM+P: Empowering Large Language Models with Optimal Planning Proficiency
verified_evidence: LLM+P maps natural-language planning problems into PDDL, delegates search to a classical planner, and translates the result back to language.
It motivates assigning formally checkable planning operations to sound external components rather than relying only on plausible generation.

sources.title: Position: LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks
verified_evidence: The position paper argues against treating autoregressive LLM generation or self-verification as a sound planner.
It proposes tighter bidirectional integration between LLMs and external model-based verifiers.

sources.title: PDDLEGO: Iterative Planning in Textual Environments
verified_evidence: PDDLEGO addresses partially observed environments by iteratively extending a formal planning representation as subgoals reveal new information.
It provides a concrete alternative to a one-shot static representation when information is initially incomplete.

sources.title: Plan-and-Act: Improving Planning of Agents for Long-Horizon Tasks
verified_evidence: Plan-and-Act separates a high-level Planner from an environment-specific Executor for long-horizon tasks.
Its dynamic variant updates the plan after executor steps because static plans can become stale or blindly persist after unexpected observations.

sources.title: DeepPlanning: Benchmarking Long-Horizon Agentic Planning with Verifiable Constraints
verified_evidence: DeepPlanning explicitly evaluates proactive information acquisition, local constrained reasoning, and global constrained optimization.
Its analysis reports omitted tool calls, difficulty with implicit environment constraints, and weak global consistency checking/backtracking over long horizons.

sources.title: Why Do LLM-based Web Agents Fail? A Hierarchical Planning Perspective
verified_evidence: The work diagnoses web agents at high-level planning, low-level execution, and replanning layers instead of relying only on end-to-end success.
It finds that more structured high-level plans can be concise and goal-directed while low-level execution remains the dominant bottleneck.
